title: Diwali ends: the lifted hill
hookLine: a hill of food stacked before dawn: Lakshmi at the door, a mountain lifted, a sister's blessing
carry: krishna shelters everyone who comes under

lines: THE LAMPS WERE ONLY THE MIDDLE.
cards: Before dawn, a temple kitchen is already roaring, while the lamps from the big night still smoke on the windowsills.
Rice, lentils, vegetables, sweets, dish after dish, carried out in steel pans and stacked on the steps in front of the image until the food is shaped like a small hill.

Children wait for their share and hear the story while they wait: a boy who once lifted a real hill. Across town, a sister is already planning tomorrow's plate for her brother. The lamps were only the middle of Diwali.

teach.b: Day three is Lakshmi puja, on the new moon itself, the night you met on day eighty-eight: the clean house, the open door, the little footprints walking in.
Ganesha is honored beside Lakshmi, and first, as always: clear the road, then begin. In Bengal it belongs to Kali, the fierce mother. Day four is Govardhan puja.
In the Bhagavata Purana, young Krishna persuaded the cowherds of Vraj to honor their own hill, Govardhan, which fed their cows, instead of the storm god Indra. Indra, offended, sent rain for days.
And Krishna lifted the whole hill with one hand, a single finger in many tellings, and held it up like an umbrella.
Everyone fit underneath: the cowherds, the children, the cows. No one was turned away. Afterward, the story says, Indra came to ask forgiveness, and Krishna was honored with a name, Govinda.
That's the teaching Govardhan puja keeps: God shelters whoever comes for refuge, and the food the earth gives is offered back with thanks.
So temples build a mountain of food, called annakut, offer it, and share it with everyone.
Day five is Bhai Dooj, for brothers and sisters. A sister marks her brother's forehead with a tilak, prays for his long life, and feeds him; he gives her a gift.

Behind it: Yama, lord of death, visited his sister Yamuna on this day and was welcomed with a meal. Diwali opened with a lamp asking Yama to pass by. It closes with Yama as a brother, sitting down to eat.

how: On the new-moon night of Diwali many Hindu families perform Lakshmi puja with Ganesha, light lamps throughout the home and draw Lakshmi's footprints at the door; the next day temples offer annakut for Govardhan puja, and on Bhai Dooj sisters mark their brothers' foreheads with tilak and share a meal.

o: a quiet monsoon fast with no lamps at all
the festival marking Rama's birth in spring
five festival days, ending with siblings at the table

games.q: the last three days — tap the pairs.
p: the new-moon night, doors left open
the hill Krishna held up like an umbrella

s: Diwali's main night falls on the full moon
Lakshmi puja is on the new moon, the darkest night of the month.
Ganesha is honored alongside Lakshmi on Diwali night
first, as always: clear the road, then begin.
Yama appears at both ends of Diwali
a lamp asks him to pass by on Dhanteras, and on Bhai Dooj he's a brother welcomed to a meal.

games.q: you're a cowherd in Vraj. the storm god is furious, and it's been pouring for days. the young Krishna says, come under here. what happens?
o: he leads everyone into a cave.
he lifts the whole hill to shelter them.
he asks Indra to stop the rain.
games.why: he holds up Govardhan like an umbrella, and everyone and their cows shelter underneath. no one is turned away. temples remember it with annakut, a mountain of food offered and shared.

practice: Before your next meal, set aside one small spoonful on a clean plate, the way annakut offers the food before anyone eats. If you pray, offer it with Krishna's name, Govinda; if not, simply thank whatever brought that food to you.
Then wish a long life to someone who once sheltered you, the way a sister does on Bhai Dooj.

wordCard.voice: Diwali. Five days of light: something new, darkness defeated, Lakshmi welcomed on the darkest night, a hill lifted to shelter everyone, and siblings at the table. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit lakṣmī: fortune, prosperity, well-being; the goddess welcomed on Diwali night.

carryVoice: Your line: Krishna shelters everyone who comes under. Diwali's five days are done. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 10.24–25 (Krishna lifts Govardhan); 10.27 (Indra's apology; Krishna honored as Govinda)
Lakshmi puja and Yama Dvitiya (Bhai Dooj), as kept in household and regional tradition
